correctness.rationale: Dark eigenvectors at zero flux are isolated and algebraically simple; the strictly dissipative bright restriction has no real eigenvalues. Exact rank-one resolvent computation gives the quadratic width -4 sin²(theta)/(n gamma). Analytic eigensplitting gives the complete survival scaling and integrated finite-dimensional spectral decomposition. Discrete Fourier orthogonality gives the closed odd/even cycle coefficients. The detector-start trace identity holds at and away from zero flux on appropriate decaying spaces. The executable verification checks 63 direct Gramians, 126 coefficient comparisons, 48 eigenvalue comparisons and 28 scaled survival profiles, supporting but not replacing the arbitrary-size proof.

value.rationale: The question is how a physically meaningful symmetry-breaking magnetic flux regularizes infinite first-absorption times caused by quantum dark states. The answer identifies an exact divergence exponent, position-dependent coefficient and complete metastable temporal profile for all cycle lengths, plus a parity-specific antipodal immunity and discontinuous detector-start mean. These structural laws distinguish geometry and monitoring behavior beyond generic perturbative expectations and motivate quantitative absorption control. No spurious independent claim is made for a general Lyapunov identity.
